## Libraries and Imports {.unnumbered .unlisted}

```python
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
```

## Model Functions {.unnumbered .unlisted}

```python
def f(x, I):                                   # rate of change of the model: x_dot = ax - bx^3 + I
    return 1.2*x - 0.8*x**3 + I                # a = 1.2, b = 0.8, I = instruction

def equilibrium_points(I):                     # finds the values of x where f(x) = 0
    coeffs = [-0.8, 0, 1.2, I]                 # coefficients of -0.8x^3 + 0x^2 + 1.2x + I (from x^3 to constant)
    roots = np.roots(coeffs)                   # all roots of the polynomial (some can be complex)
    real_roots = roots[np.isclose(roots.imag, 0)].real  # keeps only real roots: x is a real preference value
    return np.sort(real_roots)                 # sorted from smallest to largest (one real root for I = 0.70)
```


## Equilibria and Stability for $I=0$ {.unnumbered .unlisted}

```python
eq = equilibrium_points(0.0)                   # calls equilibrium_points() defined above: the 3 equilibria for I = 0

# An equilibrium is stable if f > 0 just to its left and f < 0 just to its right
stable = (f(eq - 0.01, 0.0) > 0) & (f(eq + 0.01, 0.0) < 0)  # 0.01: small enough to test each side of an equilibrium without reaching another one
```

## Rate-of-Change Graph for $I=0$ {.unnumbered .unlisted}

```python
x = np.linspace(-2, 2, 400)                    # 400 values of x between -2 and 2

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3))         # creates the figure (6 x 4 inches) and the axes
ax.plot(x, f(x, 0.0), label="f(x) = 1.2x − 0.8x³")  # draws the curve f(x), with its name in the legend
ax.axhline(0, color="black", lw=0.8)           # draws the horizontal line y = 0
ax.scatter(eq[stable], np.zeros(stable.sum()), color="black", zorder=3,
           label="Stable equilibrium")         # filled black points for stable equilibria (drawn on top of the curve)
ax.scatter(eq[~stable], np.zeros((~stable).sum()), facecolor="white",
           edgecolor="black", zorder=3,
           label="Unstable equilibrium")       # open (white) point for the unstable equilibrium

# One arrow in each of the four regions: right if f > 0, left if f < 0
for x_test in [-1.6, -0.6, 0.6, 1.6]:            # one test point in each of the 4 regions
    d = np.sign(f(x_test, 0.0))                # +1 if f > 0 (x increases), -1 if f < 0 (x decreases)
    ax.annotate("", xy=(x_test + 0.25 * d, 0), xytext=(x_test - 0.25 * d, 0),     # arrow pointing right if d = +1, left if d = -1
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color="tab:red"))

ax.set_xlabel("Coordination preference x")     # horizontal axis label
ax.set_ylabel(r"Rate of change $\dot{x}$")     # vertical axis label
ax.legend(loc="upper right")                   # shows the legend in the top-right corner
plt.show()                                     # displays the figure
```

## Simulation Settings and Initial Values {.unnumbered .unlisted}

```python
# 1. Set up the simulation

I = 0.0                                        # no external instruction
h = 0.01                                       # time step (called dt in Lab 2)
t0, t_end = 0.0, 20.0                          # start and end of the simulation
n_steps = int(round((t_end - t0) / h))         # number of Euler steps: 20 / 0.01 = 2000 (same as Lab 2)

# 2. Create the time values

t = np.linspace(t0, t_end, n_steps + 1)        # 2001 time values: 0, 0.01, 0.02, ..., 20 (the +1 is the starting point)

# 3. Prepare the arrays and starting values

x_A = np.zeros(n_steps + 1)                    # create an array of 2001 zeros, filled later with the preference over time (Pattern A side)
x_B = np.zeros(n_steps + 1)                    # array of 2001 zeros, filled later with the preference over time (Pattern B side)
x_A[0] = -1.8                                  # initial condition x(0) = -1.8
x_B[0] = 1.8                                   # initial condition x(0) = +1.8
```

## Euler Calculations for $I=0$ {.unnumbered .unlisted}

```python
# 4. Apply Euler's method

for n in range(n_steps):                       # repeat for each of the 2000 time steps
    x_A[n + 1] = x_A[n] + h * f(x_A[n], I)     # new value = old value + step size * rate of change at the old value
    x_B[n + 1] = x_B[n] + h * f(x_B[n], I)     # same Euler update for the second starting value
```

## Euler Trajectory Graph and Numerical Checks {.unnumbered .unlisted}

```python
# 5. Calculate the equilibria and determine their stability

# 0.01 is a small distance used to test stability left and right of the equilibrium

eq = equilibrium_points(I)                     # the 3 equilibria for I = 0: -1.225, 0, +1.225
stable = (f(eq - 0.01, I) > 0) & (f(eq + 0.01, I) < 0)  # True for stable equilibria (same test as Section 3)

# 6. Create the graph and plot both trajectories

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3))         # creates the figure (6 x 4 inches) and the axes
ax.plot(t, x_A, color="tab:blue", label="x(0) = -1.8")   # trajectory starting on the Pattern A side
ax.plot(t, x_B, color="tab:orange", label="x(0) = +1.8") # trajectory starting on the Pattern B side

# 7. Mark the starting values

ax.scatter([t0, t0], [x_A[0], x_B[0]], color=["tab:blue", "tab:orange"],
           zorder=3, clip_on=False)            # dots on the starting values x(0) = -1.8 and +1.8

# 8. Draw the stable and unstable equilibrium lines

for e in eq[stable]:                           # one dashed line per stable equilibrium
    ax.axhline(e, color="black", lw=0.8, ls="--")          # horizontal reference line at the stable equilibrium
ax.axhline(0, color="grey", lw=0.8)            # horizontal line x = 0 (unstable equilibrium, no preference)

# 9. Set the vertical axis ticks

ticks = [x_A[0], eq[0], eq[1], eq[2], x_B[0]]  # starting values and the 3 equilibria, all taken from the computed results
ax.set_yticks(ticks)                           # places the ticks exactly at these values
ax.set_yticklabels([str(round(float(v), 3)) for v in ticks])  # labels computed from the values, rounded to 3 decimals

# 10. Add axis labels, legend, and display the graph

ax.set_xlabel("Time t (dimensionless)")        # horizontal axis label (time has no unit in this model)
ax.set_ylabel("Coordination preference x")     # vertical axis label (same wording as Section 3)
ax.set_xlim(t0, t_end)                         # shows the whole simulation, from t = 0 to t = 20
ax.legend(loc="center right")                  # legend placed where it does not hide the curves
plt.show()                                     # displays the figure

# Numerical check
print("Number of Euler steps:", n_steps)
print("Final preference for Pattern A:", round(x_A[-1], 4)) # should be close to -1.225
print("Final preference for Pattern B:", round(x_B[-1], 4)) # should be close to +1.225
```

## Equilibrium Analysis for $I=0.70$ {.unnumbered .unlisted}

```python
# 1. Calculate the rate of change and equilibrium for I = 0.70

I_strong =  0.70 # define the positive instruction value
x_values = np.linspace(-2, 2, 400) # generate 400 equally spaced x values
eq_strong = equilibrium_points(I_strong)  # Use the function from Section 3 to find only the real equilibria

# 2. Check the stability of the equilibrium 
for x_eq in eq_strong: 
  left = f(x_eq-0.01, I_strong)
  right = f(x_eq+0.01, I_strong)
  if left > 0 and right < 0:
    stability = "Stable"
  else:
    stability = "Unstable"
  print(round(x_eq,3), stability)
```

## Rate-of-Change Graph for $I=0.70$ {.unnumbered .unlisted}

```python
# 3. Plot the curve and the equilibrium 
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3)) # create a figure and axis object
ax.plot(x_values, f(x_values, I_strong), label = "f(x) = 1.2x - 0.8x³ + 0.70") # plot the rate of change function using the x values and positive instruction defined above
ax.axhline(0, color='black', lw=0.8, linestyle='--') # plot horizontal line at y=0 to indicate where the rate of change is zero
ax.scatter(eq_strong, np.zeros(len(eq_strong)), color = 'black', label = "Stable equilibrium", zorder = 3) # plot the equilibrium point(s) on the graph

# a). Add arrows to on each side of the equilibrium to show stability
for x_test in [1.15, 1.75]: # one test point in each of the 2 regions
  direction = np.sign(f(x_test, I_strong)) # +1: right, -1: left
  ax.annotate("", xy=(x_test + 0.25 * direction, 0), # 0.25 is the length of the arrow
              xytext=(x_test - 0.25 * direction, 0),
              arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='red')) # add arrows to indicate the direction of change

# b). Add labels showing the sign of f(x) on each side of the equilibrium
ax.text(0.9, 0.3, r"f(x) > 0", ha="center")
ax.text(1.8, 0.3, r"f(x) < 0", ha="center")

# c). Add labels and legend
ax.set_xlabel("Coordination preference (x)") 
ax.set_ylabel(r"Rate of change $\dot{x}$") 
ax.legend(loc="upper right")
ax.set_xlim(-2.1, 2.1)
plt.show() 

print (eq_strong) # only one real equilibrium is calculated
```

## Euler Simulations for $I=0.70$ {.unnumbered .unlisted}

```python
# 1. Prepare the arrays using the time values from Section 4
x_A_values = np.zeros(n_steps + 1) # create empty array for starting value -1.8
x_B_values = np.zeros(n_steps + 1) # create empty array for starting value +1.8
x_A_values[0] = -1.8 # define the first value for the first array
x_B_values[0] = +1.8 # define the first value for the second array

# 2. Apply the Euler method for I = 0.70
for n in range(n_steps): # run the loop 2000 times 
  x_A_values[n + 1] = x_A_values[n] + h * f(x_A_values[n], I_strong)
  x_B_values[n + 1] = x_B_values[n] + h * f(x_B_values[n], I_strong)

# 3. Display the results
print("Final preference from -1.8:", round(x_A_values[-1], 4))
print("Final preference from +1.8:", round(x_B_values[-1], 4))
```

## Euler Trajectory Graph for $I=0.70$ {.unnumbered .unlisted}

```python
# 4. Plot both trajectories and the equilibrium
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3)) # create a figure and axis

ax.plot(t, x_A_values, color = "tab:blue", label = "x(0) = -1.8")
ax.plot(t, x_B_values, color = "tab:orange", label = "x(0) = +1.8")

ax.axhline(eq_strong[0], color="black", lw=0.8, ls = "--") # add horizontal line at the equilibrium
ax.axhline(0, color="grey", lw=0.8) # add horizontal line at y=0

ax.scatter([t0, t0], [x_A_values[0], x_B_values[0]], color = ["tab:blue" ,"tab:orange"], zorder=3, clip_on=False) # add points for the starting values

# 5. Set the y-ticks to show the starting values and the equilibrium
ticks = [x_A_values[0], 0, eq_strong[0], x_B_values[0]] # define the y-ticks to show the starting values and the equilibrium
ax.set_yticks(ticks) # set the y-ticks to the defined values

# 6. Add labels and legend
ax.set_xlabel("Time (t) dimensionless")
ax.set_ylabel("Coordination preference (x)")
ax.set_xlim(t0, t_end)
ax.legend(loc="lower right")
plt.show()
```

## Weaker Instruction Analysis for $I=0.40$ {.unnumbered .unlisted}

```python
# 1. Define the weaker positive instruction 
I_weak = 0.40 

# 2. Find the real equilibria for I = 0.40 using the function from Section 3
eq_weak = equilibrium_points(I_weak)

# 3. Check stability on both sides of each equilibrium
for x_eq in eq_weak: 
  left = f(x_eq-0.01, I_weak)
  right = f(x_eq+0.01, I_weak)
  if left > 0 and right < 0:
    stability = "Stable"
  else:
    stability = "Unstable"
  print(round(x_eq,3), stability)
```

## Comparison Graph for $I=0.40$ and $I=0.70$ {.unnumbered .unlisted}

```python
# 4. Plot both instruction conditions
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3))

ax.plot(x_values, f(x_values, I_weak), color="tab:green", label="I = 0.40") # I=0.40
ax.plot(x_values, f(x_values, I_strong), color="tab:red", label="I = 0.70") # I=0.70

# a). Mark the equilibria for I = 0.40
ax.scatter([eq_weak[0], eq_weak[2]], [0, 0], color="tab:green", zorder=3)  # Stable equilibria
ax.scatter(eq_weak[1], 0, facecolors="white", edgecolors="tab:green", zorder=3)  # Unstable equilibrium

# b). Mark the equilibrium for I = 0.70
ax.scatter(eq_strong[0], 0, color="tab:red", zorder=3) # Stable equilibria

# c). Add the horizontal line, labels, and x-axis limits
ax.axhline(0, color="black", lw=0.8, linestyle="--") # Horizontal line at y = 0

ax.set_xlabel("Coordination preference (x)")
ax.set_ylabel(r"Rate of change $\dot{x}$")
ax.legend(loc="upper right")
ax.set_xlim(-2.1, 2.1)

plt.show()
```
